identity.title: ALMA deep field in SSA22: Blindly detected CO emitters and [C II] emitter candidates
identity.journal: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan

paper_type_evidence.quote: We analyze data from the ALMA Deep Field survey of SSA22 (ADF22) observed in Band 6 in ALMA Cycle 2 in June 2014 and April 2015 (Proposal ID 2013.1.00162.S, PI: H. Umehata).

evidence.quote: ADF22 is a survey field with an area of $2' \times 3'$ centered on a $z = 3.09$ proto-cluster
ADF22 is a survey field with an area of $2' \times 3'$ centered on a $z = 3.09$ proto-cluster

question.value: Can a blind line search in the ADF22 1.1 mm ALMA survey cube find CO and [CII] emitters, and what do they imply for the [CII] luminosity function and star formation rate density at z~6?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we present a blind search for [Cii] emitters using ALMA Cycle 2 data
Proposal ID 2013.1.00162.S, PI: H. Umehata
observed in Band 6 in ALMA Cycle 2

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: four 1.875 GHz SPWs, central 263 GHz; searched 253.1–272.8 GHz

evidence.quote: The field was observed using four 1.875 GHz spectral windows (SPW) with the central frequency of 263 GHz
Line emission of [Cii] 1900.543 GHz, [Cii], CO(9-8) 1036.912 GHz and CO(4-3) 461.041 GHz
The typical angular resolution of a combined data is $0''.72 \times 0''.62$
The four SPWs have root-mean-square (RMS) noise level of 0.7, 0.7, 0.8 or 0.9 mJy beam$^{-1}$ at a 36 km s$^{-1}$ velocity resolution.
The on-source time per pointing in the fields is 4.5 min.
ALMA Cycle 2 in June 2014 and April 2015
Proposal ID 2013.1.00162.S, PI: H. Umehata
we search for their counterparts in $u^*$ band taken with the Canada France Hawaii Telescope/MegaCam
SFR-[Cii] luminosity relation (cite: delooze2014)
SFR function at $z = 6$ (cite: smit2012)
$L_{\rm IR}$ of ADF22-LineC is referred to estimation of (cite: umehata2017).
The data are analyzed with Common Astronomy Software Application (casa) ver. 4.5.3
We make continuum-subtracted datacube by using uvcontsub and clean.
The top-hat spectral smoothing window is set to be 0, 2, 4, ..., 12, 15, 18, ..., 21 slices
The details of the observation are described in (cite: umehata2017).

unstated_but_needed: clean parameters (weighting, robust, cell size, image size, threshold)

method.value: Continuum-subtract, boxcar smooth spectra, normalize each slice by RMS

evidence.quote: we normalise each slice by its RMS. We call a datacube thus-generated as “S/N cube”.

method.value: clumpfind on S/N cubes, match across smoothings, select >6 sigma and above max negative in inverted cube

evidence.quote: We select clumps that have the S/N ratio larger than $6.0 \sigma$ and also larger than the maximum negative S/N ratio measured in the inverted S/N cube
threshold value “low” of clumpfind of $\geq$ 4.5

validation.value: Compared 2014 and 2015 epochs and inverted cube

evidence.quote: We also check line spectral features of the detected clumps (sources) in the datacube separately for those observed in 2014 and 2015.

method.value: Multiwavelength counterpart search and SED fitting with hyperz

evidence.quote: We fit the SED templates by (cite: bruzual1993) to the spectral coverage from UV to 8 $\rm \mu m$, assuming a Calzetti dust extinction law
The result of SED fitting shows that reduced $\chi^2$ values becomes minimum at $z \sim 0.6-0.8$ (Figure B left).

analysis_steps.goal: Derive L[CII], SFR, LF and SFRD

method.value: L[CII] formula, De Looze SFR relation, divide mean SFR by survey volume

evidence.quote: We calculate a conservative limit of [Cii] SFRD from the mean of the SFR$_{\rm [CII]}$ of the two sources divided by the survey volume

assumptions.value: LCDM Om=0.3, OL=0.7, h=0.7; Chabrier IMF

evidence.quote: We calculate SFR assuming Chabrier initial mass function (IMF)

validation.value: Compared with UV+IR SFR upper limit

evidence.quote: The obtained SFR$_{\rm UV + FIR}$ is $<$ 30 $\rm M_\odot yr^{-1}$, being consistent with the SFR-$L_{\rm [CII]}$ relation of (cite: delooze2014)
The data are analyzed with Common Astronomy Software Application (casa) ver. 4.5.3
We use clumpfind (cite: williams1994) to search emission line sources in the S/N cube.
SED fitting is calculated by using hyperz software
The peak S/N ratio are $6.5 \sigma$, $6.2 \sigma$, $7.7 \sigma$ and $6.5 \sigma$
13$^{+4}_{-5}$ and 20$^{+9}_{-10}$ M$_\odot$/yr for ADF22-LineA and LineB
13$^{+4}_{-5}$ and 20$^{+9}_{-10}$ M$_\odot$/yr for ADF22-LineA and LineB
The derived [Cii] SFRD is $> 7.5 \times 10^{-3} \rm M_\odot yr^{-1}  Mpc^{-3}$.

findings_qualitative.value: LineC is CO(9-8) at z=3.091; LineD likely CO(4-3) at z=0.71; LineA/B likely [CII] at z=6.5/6.0

evidence.quote: two CO emitters at $z = 0.7$ and $3.1$ and two [Cii] emitter candidates at $z = 6.0$ and $6.5$

claims.hypothesis: Blind line search finds [CII] emitters at z~6
claims.experiment: clumpfind search of ADF22 S/N cubes
claims.result: Four >6 sigma candidates; two without counterparts
claims.finding: Two [CII] candidates at z=6.0 and 6.5; one may be spurious

evidence.quote: We detect four line emitter candidates with significance levels above $6 \sigma$.
Interestingly, this is close to the dust-uncorrected UV SFRD at $z = 6.2$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: LineA/B as 12CO, H2O, [NII], [OI], [OIII] emitters considered, disfavored by equivalent widths

evidence.quote: we argue that ADF22-LineA and B are more likely [Cii] emitters at $z = 6.5$ and $6.0$, rather than CO emitters at $z \leq 3.1$

limitations_admitted.value: One candidate may be spurious; LF from one source

evidence.quote: one of the two [Cii] candidates has a relatively low-$\sigma$ and thus could possibly be a spurious source

reproducibility.score_reason: Public data and recipe outline, but imaging and detection parameters are incomplete.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Imaging parameters are missing and the results are largely candidate lists.

companion_papers.why: Source of the ADF22 data and observation details
